2607.22115.title: Benchmarking Text-to-SQL under Role-Based Access Control
2607.22115.paper_summary: Given a database S and a natural language question Q, text-to-SQL systems aim to generate an SQL query that correctly answers Q when executed against S. Currently, popular text-to-SQL benchmarks mostly assume unrestricted access to S; in practice, however, user access is often restricted, e.g., through role-based access control (RBAC) policies. This leads to a potential disconnect between benchmarking results and real-world performance: an LLM with high benchmark scores might perform poorly in an access-controlled environment, by frequently violating RBAC, or rejecting a query q that could be answered with only permitted data in S. Motivated by this, we present a comprehensive text-to-SQL benchmarking framework with realistic RBAC constraints, which features an LLM-assisted workflow that augments existing text-to-SQL benchmarks with plausible user roles and access policies. To do so, we formulate the problem of role synthesis as a structured reasoning process over the database schema, in which the LLM first infers the application context from the schema, and then derives role responsibilities and access scopes consistent with this context. This process is audited by human-in-the-loop quality control, in which domain experts perform metric-guided screening on the generated roles. Besides the augmented dataset, the proposed framework also contains evaluation metrics that identify RBAC-specific failure modes, and disentangle SQL utility from access-control compliance. We apply the proposed framework to several widely-used benchmarks, and conduct a systematic empirical study of state-of-the-art text-to-SQL systems. The results show that many solutions (especially open-weight LLMs) with high benchmarking scores under an unrestricted setting suffer sharp performance degradation once access constraints are in place, due to frequent RBAC violations.
2607.22115.paper_summary_zh: 給定一個資料庫 S 和一個自然語言問題 Q，文本到 SQL 系統的目標是生成一個 SQL 查詢，當在 S 上執行時能正確回答 Q。目前，流行的文本到 SQL 基準大多假設對 S 的不受限訪問；然而在實際情況中，用戶的訪問往往受到限制，例如通過基於角色的訪問控制 (RBAC) 政策。這導致基準結果與現實世界性能之間可能存在脫節：一個在基準測試中得分高的 LLM 可能在受訪問控制的環境中表現不佳，因為它經常違反 RBAC，或拒絕一個只需使用 S 中允許的數據就能回答的查詢 q。基於此，我們提出了一個具有現實 RBAC 約束的全面文本到 SQL 基準框架，該框架具有一個 LLM 輔助的工作流程，增強了現有的文本到 SQL 基準，並引入了合理的用戶角色和訪問政策。為此，我們將角色合成問題表述為一個對資料庫架構的結構化推理過程，其中 LLM 首先從架構中推斷應用上下文，然後推導出與此上下文一致的角色責任和訪問範圍。這一過程通過人機協作的質量控制進行審核，其中領域專家對生成的角色進行指標導向的篩選。除了增強的數據集，所提出的框架還包含識別 RBAC 特定失敗模式的評估指標，並將 SQL 效用與訪問控制合規性分開。我們將所提出的框架應用於幾個廣泛使用的基準，並對最先進的文本到 SQL 系統進行了系統的實證研究。結果顯示，許多解決方案（特別是開放權重的 LLM）在不受限的設置下具有高基準得分，但一旦施加訪問限制，性能會急劇下降，這是由於頻繁的 RBAC 違規。
